authored_note: Synthea produced this patient's type 2 diabetes diagnosis, obesity, and longitudinal A1c series. The insulin regimen, the CGM training record, and the endocrinology notes that NBH-ENDO-031 section 3 turns on were authored, because Synthea does not generate records aligned to one fictional payer's numbered criteria.

problems.description: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycaemia, insulin-treated

encounters.note: Patient brought in by spouse after being found confused and diaphoretic at home. Field glucose 48 mg/dL. Treated with oral glucose gel and one ampoule of D50 with rapid resolution of symptoms. Patient reports he did not feel the usual warning symptoms before the episode and states this has happened three times since the autumn. Discharged home after two hours of observation with glucose 132 mg/dL. Endocrinology follow-up arranged. Impression: level 2 hypoglycaemia with impaired awareness on a multiple-daily-injection insulin regimen.

Fifty-nine year old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus of nine years' duration, currently on a multiple daily injection regimen: insulin glargine 38 units nightly plus insulin lispro three times daily with meals, four injections per day total, alongside metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Hemoglobin A1c today 8.6 percent, up from 8.1 percent in November. Reviewed the April emergency department visit for a glucose of 48 mg/dL. Patient confirms he no longer reliably senses hypoglycaemia and describes two further episodes since April identified only because his spouse noticed the confusion. He performs fingerstick testing but concedes he checks two to three times daily rather than the six to eight the regimen requires, citing pain in the fingertips and the demands of his work as a delivery driver, during which he cannot stop to test. Because his overnight and mid-shift excursions are going undetected, fingerstick monitoring at the frequency he is able to sustain is insufficient to guide safe titration of his mealtime insulin. Plan: prescribe a personal continuous glucose monitoring system with alerts for hypoglycaemia; refer to the diabetes education team for device training; continue current insulin doses pending sensor data; return in three months.

Completed a forty-five minute structured training session with the patient and his spouse on the use, application, calibration and interpretation of the prescribed continuous glucose monitoring system. Covered sensor insertion technique, alert threshold configuration, trend arrow interpretation, and the response protocol for a low alert. Patient demonstrated correct sensor application on a training pad and correctly interpreted four sample trend scenarios. Spouse also trained on the follower application. Training complete; patient is ready to begin monitoring once the device is dispensed.

Interim review pending device authorisation. Patient reports one further episode of hypoglycaemia in early July, again without warning symptoms, glucose 52 mg/dL on his spouse's meter. Diabetes management discussed in full: insulin regimen unchanged, fingerstick frequency unchanged at two to three per day. Reiterated that continuous monitoring is the appropriate next step and that the request remains pending with the plan.
